personality_traits: nostalgic/wistful about romance he sees in others
mildly insecure and defensive when his complaint is turned back on him
passive and low-energy in posture, letting his wife dominate the exchange
reactive rather than assertive - he opens the topic but does not control where it goes
emotional_range: wistful longing at the start, watching the other couple
gentle bewilderment while questioning their relationship ("Why don't we do that anymore?")
flat, chastened resignation by the end, tired eyes never fully brightening

0:03 brow slightly raised, mouth ajar on 'Why don't we do that anymore?' - genuine, slightly hurt curiosity
0:06 eyebrows lift, mouth small open oval on 'Like what?' - mildly defensive challenge
0:10-0:11 mouth closes, eyes remain low and heavy-lidded, no reaction shown as his wife delivers the closing line - visually deflated

characters.interactions_notes: He is the one who spots the background couple walking hand-in-hand and initiates the conversation, turning his head toward his wife to ask his questions. He never gains ground in the exchange: he sets up each beat (observation, question, incredulous 'Like what?') and she answers/deflects each time, ending the scene with the last word. His stiff, arms-hidden posture visually reinforces that he is the less dynamic, more passive half of the couple.

personality_traits: self-assured and unbothered by conventional romantic gestures
playfully teasing toward her husband, especially about his snoring and duvet-stealing
quietly confident that their unglamorous routine is its own form of intimacy
emotional_range: mildly unimpressed/knowing skepticism at the start (arms already crossed, brow arched)
soft amusement as she listens to his question
open, smiling delight on 'We do other things'
smug, narrow-eyed teasing while listing his habits (snoring, stealing the duvet)
satisfied, self-assured smile delivering the punchline 'Holding hands is nothing'
expressions: 0:00 half-lidded eyes and a faint smirk while looking past him at the other couple - already unconvinced by the comparison
0:03 closed-mouth soft smile as she listens to 'Why don't we do that anymore?'
0:04 mouth opens wide into a genuine smile/laugh on 'We do other things'

0:07-0:09 continued smirk through 'snore and steal the duvet every night', clearly enjoying calling him out
0:10-0:11 relaxed, contented smile on the closing line 'Holding hands is nothing' - the visual button of the joke
gestures: arms crossed over her chest for the entire scene - a consistent closed, confident stance that never relaxes
slight head tilt/turn toward her husband only when delivering the teasing punchline, otherwise gaze stays mostly forward or sideways
characters.interactions_notes: She holds a visible power edge over her husband throughout: her crossed-arm posture reads as composed rather than defensive, and she answers each of his prompts with a comeback that reframes the situation on her terms. She keeps her body angled slightly away/forward for most of the scene, only fully engaging him with her expression at the punchline, which lands as her 'winning' the beat both verbally and physically while he remains static and closed off beside her.
